name: Blake Dyer
bio: Blake combines field geology, carbonate geochemistry, geospatial observations, and modeling to investigate how sediments record environmental change. His research connects sea-level history, the carbon cycle, and the interpretation of sedimentary archives.

name: Argelia Silva Fragoso
bio: Argelia models seafloor lava accretion and carbon storage opportunities near ridge systems. Her work connects numerical modeling with seafloor processes.

name: Stacey Edmonsond
destination: Now a McDonnell Center for the Space Sciences Postdoctoral Fellow at Washington University in St. Louis.
bio: Stacey investigated how sedimentary and geochemical records reveal changes in Earth’s environment and carbon cycle. She led the development, testing, and documentation of StratMC, and used Bayesian inference to reconstruct the Lomagundi–Jatuli carbon-isotope excursion.

name: Miranda Reid
destination: Now a PhD candidate at the University of Waterloo.
bio: Miranda combined satellite imagery and machine learning to measure and predict coastal change in the Canadian Maritimes. Blake’s co-supervision focused on the machine-learning component of her research.

name: Connor van Wieren
bio: Connor studied Neoproterozoic carbonate chemostratigraphy and developed models investigating how sediment transport and early alteration can shape carbon-isotope records.

name: Kai Tawil-Morsink
bio: Kai investigated carbon-isotope records in Late Cenomanian and early Turonian carbonates, connecting geochemical observations to their stratigraphic context.

name: Kristyn Lang
bio: Kristyn worked on software and models for carbonate facies and sea-level inference.
